description: Dependency updates through the Mend Renovate GitHub App.

Every update is a pull request someone reads and merges by hand: no automerge. A release is proposed only once it is 3 days old, because a hijacked release is usually pulled within hours (trivy, March 2026); vulnerability alerts skip that wait and the schedule.
Commit messages follow the repository's conventional commits (chore(deps), fix(deps) for a vulnerability fix); their text is generated by the bot, in English.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Opened at once, outside the schedule and without minimumReleaseAge. Needs the repository's Dependency graph and Dependabot alerts (not Dependabot security updates).

helm-values.description: Also the values files of the charts installed only on the cloud cluster (deploy/k8s/cloud/values/), which are not named values.yaml. Their image pins are repository + tag: <version>@sha256:<digest>, or an image: string with both. The values of the platform charts and of the services are in svp-gitops, whose own Renovate configuration updates them.

customManagers.description: Tool versions with a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=... [registryUrl=...]' line right above a 'NAME := value' or 'NAME=value' line (Makefile *_VERSION).

Images pinned as <image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest> with a '# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image>' line right above (TRIVY_IMAGE, SYFT_IMAGE, COSIGN_IMAGE, OTELCOL_IMAGE, LGTM_IMAGE, k3d's helper images and registry, the k3s node image).
Values of the charts of the cloud cluster that only take a tag, so helm-values does not see them: the annotation, then 'tag: <version>@sha256:<digest>'.

Images that compose.yaml defines once as a YAML anchor (x-<name>-image: &<name>-image <image>[:<tag>]@sha256:<digest>) and services use as *<name>-image: the docker-compose manager only reads image: lines.

Charts installed only on the cloud cluster from a Helm repository: repo, chart and version of each entry of deploy/k8s/cloud/charts.json (those of the platform components, components.json, are in svp-gitops).
Charts of deploy/k8s/cloud/charts.json from an OCI registry (repo oci://<registry>/<path>): an OCI artifact, looked up as <registry>/<path>/<chart> on the docker datasource.

packageRules.description: chore(deps) for every update, also Go requires (config:recommended would make them fix(deps)); vulnerabilityAlerts above turns a vulnerability fix into fix(deps).
The project's own images in compose (svp/<service>:dev) are built locally, never pulled: nothing to look up.
Digest-only updates (an image rebuilt under the same tag) not covered by a group below: one weekly pull request.

Go modules, non-major: one pull request (go mod tidy runs after the update). A major version changes the import path and gets its own, which also rewrites the imports in the code (gomodUpdateImportPaths): without it the require line moves to /vN+1 while the code still imports /vN.

Go itself moves in one pull request with the base images of the Dockerfiles: the go/toolchain directives of go.mod, the go-version of actions/setup-go, the golang builder image (the Go of the dev machine, CI and the images stay in step).

The go directive of go.mod is the released Go that govulncheck scans and that every golang builder image must match, so Renovate has to propose raising it (it does not by default); it falls into the same group as the golang image and the go-version of actions/setup-go, so one pull request moves all three.
GitHub Actions, pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment: one pull request for non-major updates. A major gets its own pull request, since a workflow may need changes for it.

The web client's packages (web/package.json) stay exact versions: a range added later gets a pull request that pins it. web/pnpm-lock.yaml is updated with them and pnpm dedupe runs after (postUpdateOptions); pnpm reads web/pnpm-workspace.yaml, so its own 3-day wait also holds for the transitive packages the update pulls in. lockFileMaintenance stays off: it rewrites the whole lockfile without the 3-day wait.

npm packages and pnpm itself (packageManager of web/package.json), non-major: one pull request. A major gets its own, or one per monorepo (next with eslint-config-next, react with react-dom) through config:recommended.

The Sentry SDK of the web client (@sentry/nextjs) and the Sentry CLI that uploads its source maps (sentry, make web-sourcemaps) move together in one pull request, majors included: the CLI matches the bundle's chunks to their maps by the debug IDs the SDK's build plugin writes, so the two are checked as a pair (make web-sourcemaps, SVP_E2E_GLITCHTIP=1 make web-e2e). separateMajorMinor is off for them: otherwise a major of one goes to its own branch (renovate/major-sentry) while a minor of the other released with it goes to renovate/sentry.

Node moves in one pull request in web/.nvmrc (read by the Makefile, actions/setup-node and nvm), in engines of web/package.json and in the base images of deploy/docker/web.Dockerfile: the node builder image and the distroless Node runtime, whose digest updates come here too (this rule comes after the dockerfile one above).
The Node major of the distroless runtime is part of its image name (nodejs26-debian13), which Renovate never changes: it only updates the digest of the nonroot tag.
prBodyNotes: A new Node major: change the runtime image of deploy/docker/web.Dockerfile by hand in this pull request (gcr.io/distroless/nodejs<major>-debian13:nonroot, pinned by the digest of its index from docker buildx imagetools inspect), or the image keeps running the old major.

packageRules.description: Pinned tools of the Makefile and of the k3d helper scripts: one pull request.
cosign of the dev machine (COSIGN_IMAGE) and of CI (cosign-release of sigstore/cosign-installer) are the same version.

prBodyNotes: HELM_LINUX_AMD64_SHA256 in the Makefile must be changed by hand to the sha256 in helm-{{{newValue}}}-linux-amd64.tar.gz.sha256sum of the release (Renovate does not compute it); the config job of ci.yml fails until it is.
A code or rule generator changed: run make tools, then make generate (and make slo for Sloth), and commit the regenerated files; the generate job of ci.yml fails until they match.

packageRules.description: The same broker image in compose and in chart svp-data: one pull request (the redpanda chart and its values are in svp-gitops).

The Collector image of compose (otelcol, otelcol-elastic) and of make otelcol-validate (OTELCOL_IMAGE) stays the same in all three places, and the same as the cluster's (base/otel-collector.yaml of svp-gitops, which its own Renovate updates).

Elasticsearch, Kibana and APM Server of compose (profile obs-elastic) are the same version in one pull request: Kibana and APM Server refuse an older Elasticsearch, and CI only checks compose config, so a lone Kibana bump would pass CI and break make up OBS=elastic.
Charts of the cloud cluster only (Chaos Mesh, Velero): no local cluster runs them, so the check before merging is the schema check of the rendered manifests.
prBodyNotes: A chart of the cloud cluster changed: run make cloud-check before merging; it is installed only during a cloud session (stage 7).

packageRules.description: k3s: the node image of deploy/k8s/k3d.yaml and K3S_IMAGE_TAG of the Makefile (k3d's default k3s) are always the same version, in one pull request. Tags are v<major>.<minor>.<patch>-k3s<build>; the -amd64/-arm64 tags are left out. A patch is a separate update from a minor (separateMinorPatch): otherwise, once a new minor is out, Renovate proposes only that minor, which waits for approval below, and the patches of the current minor never come.

Only k3s patches open a pull request by themselves (branch renovate/patch-k3s). A new Kubernetes minor or major waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard: it moves podSecurityVersion of deploy/helm/svp-cluster/values.yaml and the three versions of deploy/k8s/pod-security-admission.yaml (make k8s-up refuses when they differ), and every component (Kyverno included) must support it.
Postgres stays on major 15, like the dev machine's Postgres and the cluster's svp-pg: a new major waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
Redis of CI stays on the dev machine's 8.8 line: a new minor or major waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard.
